explanation: Cache optimization techniques aim to improve program performance by maximizing the use of the CPU cache hierarchy (L1, L2, L3 caches).  Efficient cache usage minimizes the time-consuming access to main memory.  Strategies involve understanding data access patterns and restructuring code or data to promote temporal and spatial locality.
syntax: No single syntax; techniques involve data structure choices (e.g., arrays vs. linked lists), loop restructuring, and compiler optimization flags.
code_example: ; Example illustrating potential benefit of spatial locality
; Accessing array elements sequentially is more cache-friendly than random access
example_explanation: This assembly code example demonstrates spatial locality.  Accessing elements of `myArray` sequentially favors cache performance. The CPU likely loads a cache line containing several consecutive elements.  Subsequent accesses within the same line are faster, because they're already in the cache.  Accessing array elements randomly would cause more cache misses, resulting in slower execution.
